newsitem.title: HUNGARY: IMF says Hungary met loan pact conditions - ministry.
newsitem.headline: IMF says Hungary met loan pact conditions - ministry.

text.p: International Monetary Fund (IMF) experts visiting to Budapest found that Hungary had met the requirements of a stand-by loan agreement with the IMF, the Finance Ministry said.
The IMF granted a $381 million stand-by loan facility with a maturity of 23 months to Hungary in March.
An IMF delegation finished the second overview of the loan agreement on Tuesday. The IMF's board of directors is likely to decide on the overview in March 1997.

"The representatives of the International Monetary Fund had a favourable evaluation of the 1996 economic performance and found that it is in a complete accord with the programme," the Finance Ministry said in a statement.

The IMF found it important that the 1997 current account deficit would be lower than expected, it said, adding that the 1997 social security deficit would be larger than projected but the overall position of the state budget was as planned.

The IMF experts also agreed with the government that the monetary and economic policies approved for 1997 mean further important steps towards creating the grounds of improving economic balance and sustainable economic growth, it said.
"The delegation supported the government's 1997 economic policy targets, the current account deficit's likely position and the planned reduction of inflation," the statement added.

The IMF experts believed that inflation would not be above 18 percent in 1997. They found that the situtation was favourable for GDP and investments growth and the first signs of a faster growth had already appeared, the statement said.

The government agreed with the IMF that structural reforms should be continued and deepened. These reforms primarily aim at modernising the social security system and improving its financing, the statement said.
It added that Hungary did not intend to call down the IMF loan as it only needed the credit facility as an important seal of international support for Hungary's economic policies.
